recommended_changes: Replace unconditional 60-line, 300-module, and 20k-token limits with task-specific guidance and measured thresholds. First clarify what each limit applies to and retain any independently justified resource bound.
Replace fixed Sonnet selection with configurable model choice based on task complexity, quality, and measured cost. A model upgrade does not automatically justify removing other controls.

Replace the forced stop at 50 percent with context-management guidance: checkpoint when useful, preserve the outstanding task, and stop only when a real resource limit or user instruction requires it.
Consolidate duplicate mandatory two-phase reviews into one proportionate review path, preserving independent review where changes are high risk or evidence shows it catches distinct defects.
Trial changes incrementally and compare quality, escaped defects, review findings, latency, and cost. Six successful tasks provide a small usability signal, not a security evaluation.
preserved_boundaries: Retain permission policies and explicit authorization for destructive actions, external publication, deployment, and account changes.
Retain credential protection, untrusted-input handling, scope limits, and required verification unless a separate security evaluation supports a change.
Preserve project-specific requirements and user instructions; model capability does not supersede them.
unknowns: Meaning and original rationale of each numeric limit
Distinct defects caught by each review phase
approval_handling: These are recommendations. Security-policy changes require explicit review and authorization; do not infer their approval from the model upgrade.
